1997.question: who created / who owns the WNBA?
1997.title: wnba beginnings
items: The league was created in 1996 by the NBA - specifically by NBA commissioner David Stern and Val Ackerman, the WNBA's first president
High viewership ratings in the U.S. of the women's Olympic basketball tournament led Stern to create a pro women's league
The WNBA was created partly to supplement NBA profits
The WNBA functions more as a sub-league offshoot of the NBA than a direct sister league

1997.question: what were the O.G. brother / sister teams?
1997.title: brother and sister teams
items: The WNBA's first season had 8 teams, all owned by NBA franchises
Phoenix Suns owned the Phoenix Mercury
Los Angeles Lakers owned the Los Angeles Sparks
Sacramento Kings owned the Sacramento Monarchs
Utah Jazz owned the Utah Starzz
Houston Rockets owned the Houston Comets
New York Knicks owned the New York Liberty
Charlotte Hornets owned the Charlotte Sting
Cleveland Cavaliers owned the Cleveland Rockers

1997.question: what happened to the original 8 teams?
1997.title: THE O.G. 8
items: Of the original 8 WNBA teams the Liberty, Sparks, and Mercury are the only ones that still exist
The Utah Starzz franchise relocated to San Antonio and then to Las Vegas where they currently play as the Aces

1997.question: who were the stars of season 1?
1997.title: stars of season 1
items: Sheryl Swoopes: first player to be signed in the WNBA
Cynthia Cooper: first regular season MVP
Theresa Weatherspoon: first defensive player of the year winner
Penny Toler: scored the first field goal and free throw in the WNBA

2002.title: goodbye to strict NBA ownership rules
items: In 2002 WNBA franchises/teams could be sold to groups/cities without existing NBA franchises/teams
And WNBA teams could exist in cities with existing NBA franchises/teams without being directly affiliated with that NBA franchise/team
